source.text: Ἀπὸ δὲ ἕκτης ὥρας σκότος ἐγένετο ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.

records.literal_gloss: From then sixth hour darkness came over all the land until hour ninth.

en.L: Now from [the] sixth hour darkness came over all the land until [the] ninth hour.
en.B: At noon darkness fell over the whole land, and it lasted until three in the afternoon.
en.R: At twelve o'clock noon, the whole land became dark. It stayed dark until three o'clock in the afternoon.

fr.L: Or, depuis la sixième heure, il y eut des ténèbres sur tout le pays jusqu’à la neuvième heure.
fr.B: À partir de midi, l’obscurité se fit sur tout le pays, et elle dura jusqu’à quinze heures.
fr.R: À midi, tout le pays est devenu sombre. Il a fait noir jusqu’à trois heures de l’après-midi.

decisions.choice: the sixth hour, the ninth hour: about noon and about three in the afternoon
decisions.reason: Jews and Romans counted the hours of daylight from sunrise, about six in the morning (20:3-6).

decisions.choice: the land: the land of Israel, or the whole earth
decisions.reason: The same word can mean land or earth. Matthew does not say how far the darkness reached.

decisions.choice: darkness: a sign of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Amos 8:9 says that on that day God will make the sun go down at noon. Darkness also covered Egypt before the Passover (Exodus 10:22). Passover fell at full moon, when an eclipse of the sun cannot happen.

decisions.choice: noon, three in the afternoon (B); twelve o'clock noon, three o'clock in the afternoon (R)
alternatives: the sixth hour, the ninth hour
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the ancient way of counting the hours. Balanced and Readable give the time as we count it, as in Mark 15:33.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); speech keeps its own tenses at every level
decisions.reason: As in the rest of Matthew and in Mark 15: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, and Readable tells the story in the passé composé. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: la sixième heure, la neuvième heure (L); midi, quinze heures (B); midi, trois heures de l’après-midi (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:33-34 and Matthew 20:5 in French: Balanced uses the twenty-four-hour clock that French writes, Readable the way the hour is said in speech.

source.text: περὶ δὲ τὴν ἐνάτην ὥραν ἀνεβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγων· Ἠλὶ ἠλὶ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι;

records.literal_gloss: About then the ninth hour cried out the Jesus with voice loud saying, Eli eli lema sabachthani?

en.L: And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?"
en.B: At about three o'clock Jesus gave a loud cry: "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?"
en.R: At about three o'clock Jesus shouted loudly, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?"

fr.L: Et vers la neuvième heure, Jésus cria d’une voix forte, disant : « Éli, Éli, lema sabachthani ? »
fr.B: Vers quinze heures, Jésus poussa un grand cri : « Éli, Éli, lema sabachthani ? »
fr.R: Vers trois heures de l’après-midi, Jésus a crié très fort : « Éli, Éli, lema sabachthani ? »

decisions.choice: Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani: the first line of Psalm 22, Psalm 22:1 (22:2 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the opening of Psalm 22. The psalm moves from a cry of being forsaken to praise of God who rescues, at its end. Matthew has already echoed it in 27:35, 39 and 43.

decisions.choice: Eli ... sabachthani: the Hebrew form for my God, with an Aramaic verb
decisions.reason: Eli is close to the Hebrew of the psalm; sabachthani is Aramaic, the everyday language of Jews in Jesus's land. Mark 15:34 has the Aramaic Eloi. The sound of Eli explains why some heard the name Elijah (27:47).

decisions.choice: the spelling of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Manuscripts spell these words in several ways, some matching Mark. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani
decisions.reason: All levels keep the words in Latin letters, following the SBLGNT spelling, as Matthew keeps them and then translates them. The misunderstanding in 27:47 depends on their sound. Balanced and Readable give the hour as three o'clock, as in 27:45.

decisions.choice: Éli, Éli, lema sabachthani
decisions.reason: Matthew has the Hebrew form of "my God", so French writes "Éli", with the accent French puts on the name; it sounds like "Élie", which is what the bystanders hear in 27:47.

source.text: τοῦτ’ ἔστιν· Θεέ μου θεέ μου, ἱνατί με ἐγκατέλιπες;

records.literal_gloss: That is, God of me, God of me, why me you forsook?

en.L: That is, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: That means, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} abandoned {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: These words mean, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all alone?"

fr.L: C’est-à-dire : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} délaissé ? »
fr.B: Cela veut dire : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} abandonné ? »
fr.R: Ces mots veulent dire : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} laissé tout seul ? »

decisions.choice: my God: Jesus speaks to God
decisions.reason: Jesus addresses God and calls him "my God". Even in the cry of being forsaken he holds on to God as his own.

decisions.choice: forsaken: left behind, abandoned
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave someone alone in a time of need.

decisions.choice: the cry: Jesus's real anguish
decisions.reason: The words are a real cry of suffering, spoken in the words of Scripture. Matthew does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: my, you, me take the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: "My" and "me" are Jesus speaking of himself, and "you" is God. The first "My" starts the quoted sentence and is written plain. Readable uses plain words for forsaken.

source.text: τινὲς δὲ τῶν ἐκεῖ ἑστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ οὗτος.

records.literal_gloss: Some then of those there standing having heard were saying that Elijah calls this one.

en.L: And some of those standing there, when they heard [it], were saying, "This [man] is calling Elijah."
en.B: Hearing it, some of those who stood nearby said, "This fellow is calling for Elijah!"
en.R: Some of the people standing there heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "He is calling for Elijah!"

fr.L: Et certains de ceux qui se tenaient là, l’ayant entendu, disaient : « Celui-ci appelle Élie. »
fr.B: En l’entendant, quelques-uns de ceux qui se tenaient là dirent : « Voilà cet homme qui appelle Élie ! »
fr.R: Des gens qui étaient là {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont entendu. Ils ont dit : « Il appelle Élie ! »

decisions.choice: Elijah: the prophet God promised to send
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah before the great day of the Lord (Malachi 4:5; 3:23 in the Hebrew). Jesus spoke of this in 11:14 and 17:10-13.

decisions.choice: calling Elijah: misheard, or twisted in mockery
decisions.reason: Eli sounds like the name Elijah. Whether they misheard or twisted his words to mock him, Matthew does not say.

decisions.choice: this one: perhaps said with scorn
decisions.reason: The pronoun can carry contempt, as "this fellow" does.

decisions.choice: this fellow
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the tone of the pronoun.

source.text: καὶ εὐθέως δραμὼν εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν καὶ λαβὼν σπόγγον πλήσας τε ὄξους καὶ περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having run one of them and having taken a sponge having filled and with sour wine and having put on a reed was giving to drink him.

en.L: And immediately one of them ran and took a sponge, filled [it] with sour wine, put [it] on a reed, and was giving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a drink.
en.B: At once one of them ran and got a sponge. He soaked it in sour wine, put it on the end of a stick, and held it up for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to drink.
en.R: Right away one of them ran and got a sponge. He filled it with cheap sour wine and put it on the end of a stick. Then he held it up to Jesus's mouth so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could drink.

fr.L: Et aussitôt l’un d’eux courut, prit une éponge, [la] remplit de vin aigre, [la] mit au bout d’un roseau et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnait à boire.
fr.B: Aussitôt l’un d’eux courut prendre une éponge. Il la trempa dans du vin aigre, la fixa au bout d’un bâton et la {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tendit pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} boive.
fr.R: Tout de suite, l’un d’eux a couru chercher une éponge. Il l’a remplie de vin aigre bon marché et l’a mise au bout d’un bâton. Puis il l’a tendue jusqu’à la bouche de Jésus pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} puisse boire.

decisions.choice: sour wine: cheap wine gone sour, a common drink
decisions.reason: Soldiers and laborers drank this sharp wine mixed with water. It eased thirst.

decisions.choice: sour wine to drink: Psalm 69:21 (69:22 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: The psalm says: for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.

decisions.choice: the drink: whether kind or cruel is not clear
decisions.reason: The man may have meant to help, or to keep Jesus alive a little longer to see if Elijah came (27:49). Matthew does not say.

decisions.choice: stick
decisions.reason: As in 27:29, Balanced and Readable say stick. Readable adds "cheap" to say what kind of wine it was.

source.text: οἱ δὲ λοιποὶ ἔλεγον· Ἄφες ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας σώσων αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: The but rest were saying, Leave, let us see whether comes Elijah saving him.

en.L: But the rest were saying, "Leave [it]; let us see whether Elijah comes to save {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: But the rest told him, "Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to save {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: But the others said, "Stop! Let us wait and see if Elijah will come and save {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

fr.L: Mais les autres disaient : « Laisse ; voyons si Élie vient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sauver. »
fr.B: Mais les autres lui dirent : « Attends, voyons si Élie va venir {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sauver. »
fr.R: Mais les autres ont dit : « Arrête ! Attendons de voir si Élie va venir {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sauver. »

decisions.choice: Leave: wait, hold off
decisions.reason: The word means let go or allow. Here it most likely means hold off and wait. It may also simply introduce "let us see".

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT ends the verse here
alternatives: some important early manuscripts add: and another took a spear and pierced his side, and water and blood came out
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including two of the oldest complete copies of the Greek Bible, add these words, which are like John 19:34. They would place the piercing before Jesus died. Most manuscripts do not have them, and the SBLGNT leaves them out. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: to save him: the purpose of Elijah's coming
decisions.reason: The form shows purpose: whether Elijah comes in order to save him.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν κράξας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ἀφῆκεν τὸ πνεῦμα.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus again having cried out with voice loud let go the spirit.

en.L: And Jesus cried out again with a loud voice and yielded up [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] spirit.
en.B: Once more Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} yielded up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit.
en.R: Jesus shouted loudly again. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} spirit and died.

fr.L: Et Jésus, ayant de nouveau crié d’une voix forte, rendit l’esprit.
fr.B: Jésus poussa de nouveau un grand cri et rendit {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esprit.
fr.R: Jésus a de nouveau crié très fort. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a rendu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} esprit et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort.

decisions.choice: yielded up his spirit: let his spirit go, and so died
alternatives: his spirit was taken from him
decisions.reason: The verb means to let go or send away. The wording suggests that Jesus gave up his life himself rather than having it taken (compare 20:28; John 10:18). It may also be simply a way of saying he died.

decisions.choice: again: a second loud cry, after 27:46
decisions.reason: Matthew does not give the words of this cry.

decisions.choice: spirit: his life, his human spirit
decisions.reason: The word means breath, life or spirit. Here it is Jesus's own life given up in death.

decisions.choice: and died
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Jesus died.

decisions.choice: rendit l’esprit (L)
decisions.reason: French has the set phrase "rendre l’esprit", to die by giving up one's spirit, with the article as in the Greek, so Literal needs no supplied possessive. Balanced says "son esprit" with the span, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω εἰς δύο, καὶ ἡ γῆ ἐσείσθη, καὶ αἱ πέτραι ἐσχίσθησαν, καὶ τὰ μνημεῖα ἀνεῴχθησαν καὶ πολλὰ σώματα τῶν κεκοιμημένων ἁγίων ἠγέρθησαν, καὶ ἐξελθόντες ἐκ τῶν μνημείων μετὰ τὴν ἔγερσιν αὐτοῦ εἰσῆλθον εἰς τὴν ἁγίαν πόλιν καὶ ἐνεφανίσθησαν πολλοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, the curtain of the temple was torn from above to below into two, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split, \v 52 and the tombs were opened and many bodies of the having fallen asleep holy ones were raised, \v 53 and having come out of the tombs after the raising of him they entered into the holy city and appeared to many.

en.L: And look, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth was shaken, and the rocks were split, \v 52 and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised, \v 53 and coming out of the tombs after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} raising, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
en.B: Then the temple curtain split in two, from the top all the way to the bottom. The ground shook and rocks were torn apart. \v 52 Graves were opened, and the bodies of many of God's holy people who had fallen asleep in death were raised. \v 53 Coming out of the graves after Jesus was raised, they went into the holy city and showed themselves to many people.
en.R: At that moment the curtain in the temple was torn into two pieces, from the top to the bottom. The ground shook, and rocks split apart. \v 52 Graves broke open, and many of God's people who had died were brought back to life. \v 53 They came out of their graves. After Jesus came back to life, they went into Jerusalem, the holy city, and many people saw them.

fr.L: Et voici, le voile du sanctuaire fut déchiré en deux, du haut jusqu’en bas, et la terre fut ébranlée, et les rochers furent fendus, \v 52 et les tombeaux furent ouverts, et beaucoup de corps des saints qui s’étaient endormis furent ressuscités, \v 53 et, sortis des tombeaux après {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} résurrection, ils entrèrent dans la ville sainte et apparurent à beaucoup.
fr.B: Alors le voile du sanctuaire se déchira en deux, de haut en bas. La terre trembla et les rochers se fendirent. \v 52 Des tombeaux s’ouvrirent, et les corps de beaucoup de membres du peuple saint de Dieu, endormis dans la mort, furent ressuscités. \v 53 Sortis des tombeaux après que Jésus fut ressuscité, ils entrèrent dans la ville sainte et se montrèrent à beaucoup de gens.
fr.R: Au même moment, le grand rideau du temple a été déchiré en deux, du haut jusqu’en bas. La terre a tremblé et des rochers se sont fendus. \v 52 Des tombeaux se sont ouverts, et beaucoup de personnes du peuple de Dieu qui étaient mortes sont revenues à la vie. \v 53 Elles sont sorties de leurs tombeaux. Après que Jésus est revenu à la vie, elles sont entrées dans Jérusalem, la ville sainte, et beaucoup de gens les ont vues.

decisions.choice: the curtain of the temple: most likely the inner curtain before the Most Holy Place
alternatives: the outer curtain at the entrance
decisions.reason: The sanctuary had two great curtains. The inner one closed off the Most Holy Place, where only the high priest went once a year (Exodus 26:31-33; Hebrews 10:19-20). The outer one hung at the entrance. Matthew does not say which, or explain the sign; the passive and "from top to bottom" point to God as the one who tore it.

decisions.choice: after his raising: with coming out, or with entering the city
alternatives: the holy ones came out after Jesus rose
they came out at his death and entered the city after he rose
decisions.reason: The phrase stands between "coming out of the tombs" and "went into the holy city" and may belong with either. Either way, Jesus is the first to rise (1 Corinthians 15:20).

decisions.choice: the holy ones who had fallen asleep: faithful people of God who had died
decisions.reason: Sleep is a picture of death for those who will rise (Daniel 12:2; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-14). Ezekiel 37:12-13 pictures God opening his people's graves. Matthew does not say who these were or what became of them.

decisions.choice: the holy city: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Matthew called Jerusalem the holy city in 4:5.

decisions.choice: look (L); at that moment (R); then (B) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: after Jesus was raised (B); after Jesus came back to life (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus and use a verb instead of the noun. Readable names Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: le voile du sanctuaire (L, B); le grand rideau du temple (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as Mark 15:38 and Luke 23:45 in French, so that the three accounts read alike. "Sanctuaire" says that the curtain hung in the temple building itself (m1); Readable uses everyday words.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); membres du peuple saint de Dieu (B); personnes du peuple de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: As the New Testament term sheet sets: "les saints" at Literal, God's holy people at Balanced and Readable, since "saints" in French suggests people the Church has declared saints.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατόνταρχος καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ τηροῦντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἰδόντες τὸν σεισμὸν καὶ τὰ γενόμενα ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα λέγοντες· Ἀληθῶς θεοῦ υἱὸς ἦν οὗτος.

records.literal_gloss: The but centurion and those with him keeping watch over the Jesus having seen the earthquake and the things happening feared greatly saying, Truly God's Son was this.

en.L: And when the centurion and those with him who were keeping watch over Jesus saw the earthquake and the things that were happening, they were greatly afraid, saying, "Truly this was God's Son!"
en.B: The centurion and the men with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that was happening, and they were filled with fear. "This man truly was God's Son!" they said.
en.R: The Roman army officer and the soldiers with him were guarding Jesus. They saw the earthquake and everything else that happened, and they were very afraid. They said, "This man really was God's Son!"

fr.L: Et le centurion et ceux qui gardaient Jésus avec lui, ayant vu le tremblement de terre et ce qui arrivait, furent saisis d’une grande crainte et dirent : « Vraiment, celui-ci était Fils de Dieu ! »
fr.B: Le centurion et les hommes qui gardaient Jésus avec lui virent le tremblement de terre et tout ce qui se passait, et ils furent remplis de crainte. « Cet homme était vraiment Fils de Dieu ! » dirent-ils.
fr.R: L’officier de l’armée romaine et les soldats qui étaient avec lui gardaient Jésus. Ils ont vu le tremblement de terre et tout ce qui s’était passé, et ils ont eu très peur. Ils ont dit : « Cet homme était vraiment Fils de Dieu ! »

decisions.choice: God's Son: the Son of God
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, so it could mean "a son of God" or, from Gentiles, "a son of a god". But a title placed before the verb often lacks the article and is still definite, and the words answer the mockers' "if you are the Son of God" (27:40, 43). The disciples said the same words in 14:33. What the soldiers themselves understood is less certain.

decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: He was in charge of the execution, like the centurion of 8:5 a Gentile.

decisions.choice: greatly afraid: struck with awe
decisions.reason: The fear comes from seeing God at work, as with the disciples in 17:6.

decisions.choice: God's Son
decisions.reason: All levels say "God's Son", which keeps the openness of the Greek. Readable says "Roman army officer" for centurion, as in 8:5.

decisions.choice: Fils de Dieu, without an article, at every level; le centurion (L, B), l’officier de l’armée romaine (R)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15:39 in French: with no article the words keep the openness of the Greek (m1), as the English "God's Son" does, while the capital marks what Matthew means by them. Readable names the centurion as the English does.

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐκεῖ γυναῖκες πολλαὶ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, αἵτινες ἠκολούθησαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας διακονοῦσαι αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: Were then there women many from afar watching, who followed the Jesus from the Galilee serving him;

en.L: And many women were there, watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};
en.B: A number of women stood watching from far off. These women had come with Jesus all the way from Galilee, providing for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Many women were there too. They watched from far away. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to help {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and take care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Or il y avait là beaucoup de femmes qui regardaient de loin, elles qui avaient suivi Jésus depuis la Galilée en {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servant ;
fr.B: Beaucoup de femmes étaient là aussi, qui regardaient de loin. Elles avaient accompagné Jésus depuis la Galilée et pourvoyaient à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} besoins.
fr.R: Beaucoup de femmes étaient là aussi. Elles regardaient de loin. Elles avaient suivi Jésus depuis la Galilée pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}aider et s’occuper de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

decisions.choice: serving him: providing for his needs
decisions.reason: The verb means to serve or wait on. Luke 8:3 says such women provided for Jesus from their own means.

decisions.choice: the women stayed when the disciples fled
decisions.reason: All the disciples had left him and fled (26:56). The women watch his death, his burial (27:61) and the empty tomb (28:1).

decisions.choice: from a distance: perhaps Psalm 38:11 (38:12 in the Hebrew numbering)
decisions.reason: The psalm says that friends and neighbors stand far off. Matthew does not cite it.

source.text: ἐν αἷς ἦν Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰωσὴφ μήτηρ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου.

records.literal_gloss: among whom was Mary the Magdalene and Mary the of James and Joseph mother and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.

en.L: among whom were Mary the Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
en.B: Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee's sons.
en.R: Mary from the town of Magdala was there. So was Mary, the mother of James and Joseph. The mother of James and John, the sons of Zebedee, was there too.

fr.L: parmi lesquelles étaient Marie la Magdaléenne, et Marie, la mère de Jacques et de Joseph, et la mère des fils de Zébédée.
fr.B: Parmi elles se trouvaient Marie de Magdala, Marie, mère de Jacques et de Joseph, et la mère des fils de Zébédée.
fr.R: Marie, de la ville de Magdala, était là. Il y avait aussi Marie, la mère de Jacques et de Joseph. La mère de Jacques et de Jean, les fils de Zébédée, était là, elle aussi.

decisions.choice: Mary the Magdalene: Mary from Magdala
decisions.reason: Magdala was a town on the west shore of the Sea of Galilee. Luke 8:2 says seven demons had gone out of her.

decisions.choice: Mary the mother of James and Joseph: most likely not Jesus's mother
decisions.reason: Jesus had brothers named James and Joseph (13:55), but Matthew would hardly name Jesus's mother this way here. Mark 15:40 calls this Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses.

decisions.choice: the mother of Zebedee's sons: the mother of James and John
decisions.reason: She asked Jesus for places at his right and left (20:20-21). Mark 15:40 names a Salome among the women; she may be the same person.

decisions.choice: from the town of Magdala; James and John
alternatives: the Magdalene; the sons of Zebedee
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name and names the sons of Zebedee (4:21).

decisions.choice: Marie la Magdaléenne (L); Marie de Magdala (B, R) (for the whole of Matthew 27-28)
decisions.reason: As in Mark 15-16 and Luke 24 in French. Literal keeps the Greek adjective; Balanced and Readable name her town, which is what the word means (m1). "Marie-Madeleine" is the church name and hides the place.

source.text: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης ἦλθεν ἄνθρωπος πλούσιος ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας, τοὔνομα Ἰωσήφ, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐμαθητεύθη τῷ Ἰησοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Evening then having come came a man rich from Arimathea, the name Joseph, who also himself was discipled to the Jesus;

en.L: And when evening had come, a rich man from Arimathea came, named Joseph, who himself also had become a disciple of Jesus;
en.B: As evening came on, Joseph arrived, a rich man from the town of Arimathea who had also become one of Jesus's disciples.
en.R: That evening a rich man named Joseph came. He was from the town of Arimathea. He had also become a follower of Jesus.

fr.L: Or, le soir étant venu, vint un homme riche d’Arimathée, nommé Joseph, qui était lui aussi devenu disciple de Jésus ;
fr.B: Le soir venu, arriva Joseph, un homme riche de la ville d’Arimathée, qui était lui aussi devenu disciple de Jésus.
fr.R: Ce soir-là, un homme riche appelé Joseph est arrivé. Il venait de la ville d’Arimathée. Lui aussi était devenu disciple de Jésus.

decisions.choice: evening: the late afternoon before sunset, with the Sabbath near
decisions.reason: The law said a body hanged on a tree must not stay there overnight (Deuteronomy 21:22-23), and the Sabbath began at sunset (27:62).

decisions.choice: Arimathea: a town in Judea
decisions.reason: Luke 23:51 calls it a town of the Jews. Its exact location is not certain.

decisions.choice: a rich man: perhaps Isaiah 53:9
decisions.reason: The servant in Isaiah 53:9 is with a rich man in his death. Matthew does not cite the verse.

decisions.choice: had become a disciple: had been taught by Jesus and followed him
decisions.reason: The verb means to be made a disciple (28:19). John 19:38 says Joseph followed Jesus in secret.

decisions.choice: follower
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for disciple, as elsewhere in Matthew.

decisions.choice: disciple at Readable too (also 28:7-8, 28:13, 28:16)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Matthew in French: "disciple" is a common French word, so Readable keeps it where the English Readable says "follower".

source.text: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This one having gone to the Pilate asked for the body of the Jesus.

en.L: He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
en.B: He went to Pilate and requested Jesus's body.
en.R: Joseph went to Pilate and asked him for Jesus's body.

fr.L: Celui-ci alla trouver Pilate et demanda le corps de Jésus.
fr.B: Il se rendit auprès de Pilate et lui demanda le corps de Jésus.
fr.R: Joseph est allé voir Pilate et lui a demandé le corps de Jésus.

decisions.choice: asked for the body: permission was needed
alternatives: the body would have been given anyway
decisions.reason: Romans often left the bodies of the crucified on the cross or threw them in a common grave. To ask for the body of a man executed for rebellion took courage (Mark 15:43).

decisions.choice: Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable names Joseph.

source.text: τότε ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐκέλευσεν ἀποδοθῆναι.

records.literal_gloss: Then the Pilate ordered to be given.

en.L: Then Pilate ordered [it] to be given [to him].
en.B: Pilate then ordered that it be handed over to him.
en.R: Pilate gave orders for the body to be given to Joseph.

fr.L: Alors Pilate ordonna qu’[il lui] soit remis.
fr.B: Pilate ordonna alors qu’on le lui remette.
fr.R: Pilate a donné l’ordre de donner le corps à Joseph.

decisions.choice: to be given: to be handed over to Joseph
alternatives: to be given back to the family
decisions.reason: The verb means to give over or give back. Pilate releases the body to Joseph.

decisions.choice: the body; to Joseph
decisions.reason: Readable says what was given and to whom.

source.text: καὶ λαβὼν τὸ σῶμα ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι καθαρᾷ, καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸ ἐν τῷ καινῷ αὐτοῦ μνημείῳ ὃ ἐλατόμησεν ἐν τῇ πέτρᾳ, καὶ προσκυλίσας λίθον μέγαν τῇ θύρᾳ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπῆλθεν.

records.literal_gloss: And having taken the body the Joseph wrapped it in a linen cloth clean, \v 60 and placed it in the new of him tomb which he had hewn in the rock, and having rolled a stone great to the door of the tomb he went away.

en.L: And Joseph took the body and wrapped it in clean linen cloth \v 60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had cut in the rock; and having rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb, he went away.
en.B: Joseph took the body and wound a clean linen sheet around it. \v 60 Then he placed it in the new tomb he had carved in the rock for himself, rolled a great stone across the doorway of the tomb, and went away.
en.R: Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean cloth made of linen. \v 60 He put the body in his own new tomb, which had been cut into the rock. Then he rolled a big stone in front of the opening to close the tomb, and he went away.

fr.L: Et Joseph, ayant pris le corps, l’enveloppa dans un drap de lin propre \v 60 et le déposa dans son tombeau neuf, qu’il avait taillé dans le roc ; et, ayant roulé une grande pierre contre la porte du tombeau, il s’en alla.
fr.B: Joseph prit le corps et l’enveloppa dans un drap de lin propre. \v 60 Puis il le déposa dans le tombeau neuf qu’il s’était fait tailler dans le roc, roula une grande pierre devant l’entrée du tombeau et s’en alla.
fr.R: Joseph a pris le corps et l’a enveloppé dans un drap propre, fait de lin. \v 60 Il a mis le corps dans son propre tombeau, un tombeau neuf qu’on avait creusé dans le rocher. Puis il a roulé une grosse pierre devant l’ouverture pour fermer le tombeau, et il est parti.

decisions.choice: clean linen: a fresh linen sheet for burial
decisions.reason: The dead were wrapped in linen cloth. A clean, new cloth showed honor to the dead.

decisions.choice: his own new tomb cut in the rock: a family tomb no one had used
decisions.reason: Wealthy families in Jerusalem had tombs cut into the rock, with shelves for bodies inside. Luke 23:53 and John 19:41 say no one had yet been laid in it.

decisions.choice: a great stone at the door: a large stone that closed the entrance
decisions.reason: Such stones were often round and rolled in a groove across the doorway. It will be sealed and guarded (27:66) and rolled away (28:2).

decisions.choice: it, for the body
decisions.reason: The Greek pronoun is neuter and refers to the body. It is not a pronoun for Jesus himself, so it takes no setting.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ἐκεῖ Μαριὰμ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ ἡ ἄλλη Μαρία καθήμεναι ἀπέναντι τοῦ τάφου.

records.literal_gloss: Was then there Mary the Magdalene and the other Mary sitting opposite the tomb.

en.L: And Mary the Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
en.B: Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary too, seated facing the tomb.
en.R: Mary from Magdala and the other Mary were there. They were sitting across from the tomb.

fr.L: Or Marie la Magdaléenne était là, et l’autre Marie, assises en face du tombeau.
fr.B: Marie de Magdala était là, et l’autre Marie aussi, assises face au tombeau.
fr.R: Marie de Magdala et l’autre Marie étaient là. Elles étaient assises en face du tombeau.

decisions.choice: the other Mary: the mother of James and Joseph
decisions.reason: She is the second Mary named in 27:56. The two women will come back to the tomb in 28:1.

decisions.choice: sitting opposite the tomb: they saw where he was laid
decisions.reason: The women see the place of burial, so they know which tomb they find empty (28:1, 6).

decisions.choice: Mary: a second spelling of the same name in the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT spells Mary Magdalene's name in a slightly different form here than in 27:56. It is the same name and the same woman.

source.text: Τῇ δὲ ἐπαύριον, ἥτις ἐστὶν μετὰ τὴν παρασκευήν, συνήχθησαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι πρὸς Πιλᾶτον λέγοντες· Κύριε, ἐμνήσθημεν ὅτι ἐκεῖνος ὁ πλάνος εἶπεν ἔτι ζῶν· Μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἐγείρομαι·

records.literal_gloss: The then next day, which is after the Preparation, were gathered together the chief priests and the Pharisees before Pilate \v 63 saying, Sir, we remembered that that deceiver said while living, After three days I am raised.

en.L: And on the next day, which is after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate \v 63 and said, "Sir, we have remembered that that deceiver said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still living, 'After three days I am raised.'
en.B: On the following day, the one after the day of Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees came together to Pilate. \v 63 "Sir," they said, "we have remembered something that impostor said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still alive: 'After three days I will be raised.'
en.R: The next day was the Sabbath, the day after Preparation Day. The leading priests and the Pharisees went to Pilate together. \v 63 They said, "Sir, we remember something that liar said while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was still alive. He said, 'After three days I will come back to life.'

fr.L: Or le lendemain, qui est après la Préparation, les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens se rassemblèrent auprès de Pilate \v 63 et dirent : « Seigneur, nous nous sommes souvenus que ce trompeur a dit, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore vivant : “Après trois jours, je ressuscite.”
fr.B: Le lendemain, c’est-à-dire le jour qui suivait la Préparation, les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens se rendirent ensemble chez Pilate. \v 63 « Seigneur, dirent-ils, nous nous sommes souvenus que cet imposteur a dit, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore en vie : “Après trois jours, je ressusciterai.”
fr.R: Le lendemain, c’était le sabbat, le jour qui suit la Préparation. Les chefs des prêtres et les Pharisiens sont allés ensemble voir Pilate. \v 63 Ils lui ont dit : « Gouverneur, nous nous rappelons ce que ce menteur a dit quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était encore vivant. Il a dit : “Après trois jours, je reviendrai à la vie.”

decisions.choice: the day after the Preparation: the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Preparation was the day before the Sabbath, the Friday on which Jesus died. The next day was the Sabbath itself.

decisions.choice: deceiver: one who leads people astray
decisions.reason: The word means one who misleads. Jesus warned that false messiahs would lead many astray (24:4-5, 24); his enemies call him one.

decisions.choice: I am raised: the present for a sure future; it can mean I rise or I am raised
decisions.reason: Jesus foretold that he would be raised on the third day (16:21; 17:23; 20:19). The leaders quote the promise to guard against it.

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address
alternatives: Lord, as a confession of faith
decisions.reason: The word is the same as "Lord", but spoken to Pilate it is a title of respect.

decisions.choice: The next day was the Sabbath
decisions.reason: Readable says which day it was. Pronouns for Jesus take the deity_pronoun setting even in his enemies' words; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plain.

decisions.choice: Seigneur (L, B); Gouverneur (R); "tu" to Pilate at every level
decisions.reason: The address is a polite title (m4). "Monsieur" is too slight for a Roman governor, and "Excellence" sits badly with "tu"; "Seigneur" is the old French address to a man in power, and Readable uses his office instead. The Greek command is singular, so the priests say "tu" (style guide §6).

decisions.choice: ce trompeur (L); cet imposteur (B); ce menteur (R)
decisions.reason: The word means one who leads people astray (m2). "Séducteur" now suggests romance; Literal says "trompeur", Balanced the usual word for a false claimant, Readable the plain word the English uses.

source.text: κέλευσον οὖν ἀσφαλισθῆναι τὸν τάφον ἕως τῆς τρίτης ἡμέρας, μήποτε ἐλθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ κλέψωσιν αὐτὸν καὶ εἴπωσιν τῷ λαῷ· Ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἔσται ἡ ἐσχάτη πλάνη χείρων τῆς πρώτης.

records.literal_gloss: Command therefore to be secured the tomb until the third day, lest having come the disciples of him they steal him and say to the people, He was raised from the dead, and will be the last deception worse than the first.

en.L: So command that the tomb be made secure until the third day, so that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples do not come and steal {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and say to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead,' and the last deception will be worse than the first."
en.B: Give the command, then, to have the tomb guarded securely until the third day. If not, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples could come, take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away by stealth, and announce to the people, 'He has been raised from the dead.' And this final fraud would do more harm than the first one."
en.R: So please give orders for the tomb to be guarded until the third day. If you do not, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers might come and steal {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body. Then they would tell the people, 'He has come back from death!' This last lie would be even worse than the first one."

fr.L: Ordonne donc que le tombeau soit mis en sûreté jusqu’au troisième jour, de peur que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples ne viennent {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voler et ne disent au peuple : “Il a été ressuscité des morts”, et la dernière imposture sera pire que la première. »
fr.B: Donne donc l’ordre de garder le tombeau en sûreté jusqu’au troisième jour. Sinon, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples pourraient venir {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}enlever en secret, puis annoncer au peuple : “Il a été ressuscité des morts.” Et cette dernière tromperie ferait plus de mal que la première. »
fr.R: Alors, s’il te plaît, donne l’ordre de faire garder le tombeau jusqu’au troisième jour. Sinon, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples risquent de venir voler {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps. Ensuite, ils diraient aux gens : “Il est revenu de la mort !” Ce dernier mensonge serait encore pire que le premier. »

decisions.choice: the last deception, the first: a report of resurrection would be worse than his claims while alive
decisions.reason: The first deception, as the leaders see it, is Jesus's own claim to be the Messiah and the Son of God (26:63-64). The last would be the news that he rose.

decisions.choice: until the third day: counting the day of his death as the first
decisions.reason: The third day was the day after the Sabbath, the day of 28:1.

decisions.choice: steal him: carry off his body
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of Jesus himself, though they mean the body.

decisions.choice: his body
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the leaders mean his body. The pronoun still refers to Jesus and takes the setting.

source.text: ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ἔχετε κουστωδίαν· ὑπάγετε ἀσφαλίσασθε ὡς οἴδατε.

records.literal_gloss: Said to them the Pilate, You have a guard; go, make secure as you know.

en.L: Pilate said to them, "You have a guard; go, make [it] as secure as you know [how]."
en.B: Pilate told them, "You may have a guard. Go and secure it in whatever way you think best."
en.R: Pilate said, "You can have some soldiers. Go and guard the tomb the best way you know."

fr.L: Pilate leur dit : « Vous avez une garde ; allez, mettez[-le] en sûreté comme vous savez [le faire]. »
fr.B: Pilate leur répondit : « Vous pouvez avoir une garde. Allez, et protégez le tombeau comme vous le jugerez bon. »
fr.R: Pilate a dit : « Vous pouvez prendre des soldats. Allez garder le tombeau du mieux que vous pouvez. »

decisions.choice: you have a guard: take a guard of soldiers
alternatives: you have your own temple guard
decisions.reason: The verb can be a statement or a command. The guards later report to the chief priests (28:11), which could suit the temple police; but the leaders promise to keep them out of trouble with the governor (28:14), which suits Roman soldiers.

decisions.choice: guard: a group of soldiers on watch
decisions.reason: The word comes from Latin and names a detachment of guards.

decisions.choice: You may have (B); You can have (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the reading as a command or permission, which the meaning decision marks as uncertain.

source.text: οἱ δὲ πορευθέντες ἠσφαλίσαντο τὸν τάφον σφραγίσαντες τὸν λίθον μετὰ τῆς κουστωδίας.

records.literal_gloss: They then having gone made secure the tomb having sealed the stone with the guard.

en.L: So they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone along with the guard.
en.B: They went and sealed the stone, and with the guard in place they made the tomb secure.
en.R: So they went to the tomb. They put a seal on the stone, and they left soldiers there to guard it.

fr.L: Et eux, s’en étant allés, mirent le tombeau en sûreté, en scellant la pierre, avec la garde.
fr.B: Ils s’en allèrent, scellèrent la pierre et, avec la garde postée là, mirent le tombeau en sûreté.
fr.R: Alors ils sont allés au tombeau. Ils ont mis un sceau sur la pierre, et ils ont laissé des soldats pour le garder.

decisions.choice: sealing the stone: a cord or wax seal, so that tampering would show
decisions.reason: A seal across the stone and the rock would be broken if anyone moved it (compare Daniel 6:17).

decisions.choice: with the guard: by posting the guard as well
decisions.reason: The tomb was made secure in two ways: by the seal and by the soldiers.
